The Divisional Manager vs Reena Behera & Others on 10 March,
2025
Author: Biraja Prasanna Satapathy

Bench: Biraja Prasanna Satapathy
 In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
 Maca No.447 of 2019
 The Divisional Manager, ... Appellant
 Oriental Insurance Company
 Ltd.
 Mr. A.A. Khan, Advocate
 -versus-
 Reena Behera & Others ... Respondents

entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Mr. P.K. Nayak, Advocate
 for Respondent Nos.1 & 2

Coram:
 Justice Biraja Prasanna Satapathy
 Order
10.03.2025 Order No.
20. 1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical Mode).
2.
The present appeal has been filed by the appellant challenging the judgment dated 31.08.2018 so passed by the learned 3rd MACT, Talcher in M.A.C. No.39 of 2016.

Vide the said judgment, learned Tribunal allowed the claim application of the claimants/respondents no.1 & 2 by directing the appellant to pay compensation amount of Rs.5,23,000/- along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application till its realization.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that since the deceased was riding the motor cycle registered in the name of respondent no.3 and the said accident never occurred in course of employment, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in AIR 2020 SC 527 (Ramkhiladi & Others Vrs. The United India Insurance Company and Others),
claimants/respondent nos.1 & 2 are not entitled to get any compensation.

sentences.text: While answering the finding recorded by the learned Tribunal on Issue No. 2, it appears that, as such, the learned Tribunal has not at all answered the aforesaid issue.
While answering Issue No. 2, there is no specific finding whether the deceased - driver was in employment of the opponent owner Bhagwan Sahay or not.
Even otherwise, no evidence is led by the claimants to prove that the deceased driver was in employment of the opponent owner Bhagwan Sahay.

Despite the above, while answering Issue No. 4 there is some observation made by the learned Tribunal that the deceased driver was in employment of the opponent owner Bhagwan Sahay,
which is not supported by any evidence on record.

Under the circumstances, the deceased driver cannot be said to be in employment of the opponent owner Bhagwan Sahay and, therefore, he can be said to be permissible user and/or borrower of motor vehicle owned by the opponent owner Bhagwan Sahay.
With these findings, the main question posed for consideration of this Court referred to hereinabove is required to be considered.

5.6 In view of the above and for the reasons stated above, in the present case, as the claim under Section 163A of the Act was made only against the owner and insurance company of the vehicle which was being driven by the deceased himself as borrower of the vehicle from the owner of the vehicle and he would be in the shoes of the owner, the High Court has rightly observed and held that such a claim was not maintainable and the claimants ought to have joined and/or ought to have made the claim under Section163A of the Act against the driver, owner and/or the insurance company of the offending vehicle i.e. RJ 29 2M 9223 being a third party to the said vehicle.
5.8 However, at the same time, even as per the contract of insurance, in case of personal accident the ownerd river is entitled to a sum of Rs.1 lakh.
Therefore, the deceased, as observed hereinabove, who would be in the shoes of the owner shall be entitled to a sum of Rs.1 lakh, even as per the contract of insurance.

However, it is the case on behalf of the original claimants that there is an amendment to the 2 nd Schedule and a fixed amount of Rs.5 lakh has been specified in case of death and therefore the claimants shall be entitled to Rs.5 lakh.
The same cannot be accepted.

In the present case, the accident took place in the year 2006 and even the Judgment and Award was passed by the learned Tribunal in the year 2009, and the impugned Judgment and Order has been passed by the High Court in 10.05.2018, i.e. much prior to the amendment in the 2nd Schedule.
In the facts and circumstance of the present case, the claimants shall not be entitled to the benefit of the amendment to the 2nd Schedule.
At the same time, as observed hereinabove, the claimants shall be entitled to Rs.1 lakh as per the terms of the contract of insurance, the driver being in the shoes of the owner of the vehicle.

3.1. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that since the deceased was not riding the motor cycle while in course of employment, claim application filed under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, 1988 is not maintainable.

But learned Tribunal without The Divisional Manager vs Reena Behera & Others on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87698526/
2 proper appreciation, allowed the clam application vide the impugned judgment.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3.2 It is also contended that in view of the evidence laid by P.W.2 before the learned Tribunal, who happens to be an eye witness, no liability could have been saddled on the appellant company.
It is accordingly contended that the impugned judgment is not sustainable in the eye of law.

4. Mr. P.K. Nayak, learned counsel for the respondent nos.1 & 2 though supported the impugned judgment, but in course of hearing, contended that liberty may be given to the respondent nos.1 & 2 to approach the authority of Gohira Dam as the deceased died due to the illegal action of Gohira Dam authority.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the respective parties and placing reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court as cited supra, this Court is of the view that no liability could have been saddled on the appellant Company in entertaining the application filed under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, 1988.
In view of the decision cited supra, application under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, 1988 was not at all entertainable also.

However, considering the submission of the learned counsel appearing for the claimants/respondent nos.1 & 2, this Court while quashing the impugned judgment dated 31.08.2018 so passed by the learned 3rd MACT, Talcher in M.A.C. No.39 of 2016, grants liberty to the claimants/respondent nos.1 & 2 to raise their claims for compensation before the authorities of Gohira Dam.
6. The MACA is accordingly disposed of.

(Biraja Prasanna Satapathy) Judge amit Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA,
